cards.headline: The devil got into me at Toe Rag
cards.snippet: The song was written in the studio. The White Stripes were recording Elephant at Toe Rag in Hackney, London, in the spring of 2002 when, in Jack White's words, “it was as if the devil got into me and I could not hear anything except guitars — fat, dirty, ear-destroying guitar sounds.” The title came from an STC microphone used at the studio, nicknamed the Ball and Biscuit. At 7 minutes 18 seconds, built on a traditional 12-bar blues, it is the longest studio recording the duo ever made.
cards.context: Elephant was cut in about two weeks at Toe Rag on pre-1963 equipment — and this track was written in the room itself.

cards.headline: A seventh son, making fun of cockiness
cards.snippet: Its singer is a self-proclaimed seventh son, courting a woman who could care less and telling her it is “quite possible” that he is her third man. The claim was autobiography: Jack White is the seventh and final son in a family of ten children. He said he wanted the song to be “making fun of cockiness”. Critics took the boast at face value — The Washington Post called it “perhaps the White Stripes' definitive statement”, and a 2012 Rolling Stone readers' poll voted it his greatest recording “by a landslide”.
cards.context: Willie Dixon's “The Seventh Son” is the song's named model — Jack built his boast on the older bluesman's.

cards.headline: An AI visualizer, for this band?
cards.snippet: A bit weird to have an AI generated visualizer when The White Stripes were so engaged in anti-digital process.
cards.context: It's the top comment on the official visualizer upload; the fifty replies under it argue both sides.

replies.author: @raydeeffect6685
replies.text: Jack is incredibly into juxtaposition. I also think the simplicity of creating using AI is also what drew him. Or it could've been someone else's idea entirely with Jack's approval.

cards.headline: The mailbox, the breakfast, twenty years
cards.snippet: I met my husband 20 years ago. He drove me home in the wee hours of the morning, and proceeded to take out my mailbox. This was playing in the car. Then I made him a full English breakfast which we ate on my front lawn. Together ever since. ❤️
cards.context: A first night twenty years ago, with this song playing in the car — and they have been together ever since.

cards.headline: The night Dylan sang it in Detroit
cards.snippet: On 17 March 2004, at the State Theatre in Detroit, Bob Dylan brought Jack White out for a surprise encore and sang White's own song with him — one of only one or two songs from this century that Dylan has ever covered. It circulated as a bootleg for almost twenty years before Third Man Records released a soundboard recording as a 7-inch single in 2023. One listener: “This audio recording is proof that God exists, and that he loves us.”
cards.context: Third Man paired it on the 7-inch with the White Stripes' own first live performance of the song, London, 2002.

version.versionLabel: Bob Dylan live in Detroit with Jack White (2004)

cards.headline: Two days' notice on SNL
cards.snippet: Called in on two days' notice to replace Morgan Wallen on Saturday Night Live on 10 October 2020, Jack White opened with his Beyoncé collaboration “Don't Hurt Yourself”, slid into this song, and reworked it with lyrics from Blind Willie Johnson's “Jesus Is Coming Soon” — a gospel song about the 1918 flu, sung in the middle of another pandemic. One listener: “Best thing that happened in 2020.”
cards.context: He learned he had the slot on the Friday and played it on the Saturday, with Daru Jones and Dominic Davis.

version.versionLabel: Jack White on Saturday Night Live (2020)

cards.headline: Live in Tokyo, 2003
cards.snippet: Camcorder footage from the band's third trip to Japan — Shibuya-AX, Tokyo, 22 October 2003 — that stayed unreleased until October 2020, when it was put out ahead of The White Stripes Greatest Hits. One listener: “Man just when you think you hear the best version there is, another pops up”
cards.context: Shot on the band's third Japanese tour, seven months after Elephant's release.

version.versionLabel: The White Stripes live at Shibuya-AX, Tokyo (2003)

cards.headline: Heard at the beginning
cards.snippet: David Fincher's film opens in a bar near Harvard, where Erica Albright is breaking up with Mark Zuckerberg — and this song is playing in the background. It is the first music heard in the film, under the conversation that sets the whole story in motion.
cards.context: The film was selected for the US National Film Registry in 2024, as culturally and historically significant.
